Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has flagged a couple of items we need to close before legal can sign off for Dedicated:

Hi Rajiv —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by next steps:

- Region pinning: yes — we support tenant pinning to a single region for Dedicated. By default there is no cross-region replication unless configured as part of a DR policy.
- Isolation: we provide host affinity (rack and host tags) plus network VPC isolation for Dedicated pools. Logical isolation (tenant scoping) is enforced in the runtime layer and on disk via tenant-scoped volumes.
- Deletion evidence: we can produce sanitized audit logs showing snapshot deletion and a chain-of custody; irreversible deletion timelines depend on snapshot retention and backup windows but typical turnaround for the wipe path is 24–72 hours after request and confirmation.
- Routing: we can produce a routing attestation and a sanitized tenant-routing audit log that shows egress endpoints and region bindings.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura (cc) will produce the sanitized evidence bundle (logs + short runbook) and a diagram of the site-anchoring topology.
2) I will coordinate an attestation letter and a DocuSign envelope for your legal team.
3) Ben can push a sample tenant-routing audit log (redacted) with timestamps.

Can you confirm the legal contact and whether the logs need additional redaction for IPs? Once you confirm, we’ll aim to get the bundle to you within 24 business hours.

— Sergio

Rajiv —

Adding technical detail so procurement has clear language for the SOW:

1) Region pinning mechanics
- Tenant is assigned to a Dedicated GPU pool scoped to a single cloud region. The assignment is enforced by orchestration tags at provisioning time; these tags prevent scheduler placement outside the tagged region.
- Control plane operations that might create replicas (backups, snapshots) run in the same region unless a customer explicitly requests cross-region replication for DR.

2) Physical vs logical isolation
- Physical: host affinity + rack labeling, and Dedicated pools are logically mapped to physically separate allocation groups to reduce noisy neighbor risk. We can provide a host-affinity manifest (redacted) showing the allocation boundaries.
- Logical: tenancy enforced by tenant-id namespaces, LUKS-encrypted volumes per tenant, and per-tenant KMS key encryption. We do not co-mount tenant volumes across tenants.

3) Snapshot / backup deletion flow
- Deletion request -> mark snapshot tombstoned (0–2 hours) -> background sweep job purges snapshot objects from object storage (24–72 hours depending on size and system load) -> metadata finally removed and a purge-event is emitted to audit logs.
- For legal/compliance we can produce an event trail: request received, tombstone timestamp, purge-complete timestamp and a checksum of destroyed objects.

4) Routing and egress assurance
- All egress for the tenant's Dedicated pool is via region-local NAT/gateway devices bound to the region. There is no cross-region egress for pinned tenants.
- We can provide a sanitized tenant-routing audit log that shows the path with time-aligned entries (we will redact internal IPs and hostnames).

Attachments I will include in the bundle: a short runbook (blueharbor_residency_qna_v2.pdf) and a topology diagram (site-anchoring-diagram.png). Ben — please include the sample tenant-routing-audit.log (redacted) when you send.

If BlueHarbor needs an SLA amendment for absolute physical host exclusivity or dedicated rack allocation, we can scope that in the Dedicated contract (that would be an additional commitment and pricing item).

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, Security & Compliance
